done.why: I reached the Carousel Room with eight identical exits and stopped. I'd seen the main idea and didn't want to wander a maze.

about: A cave-exploring game that felt like a Zork sequel. A wizard shows up now and then and conjures things such as a basilisk and a book, which turn out not to be real.

moments.note: 'cross the bridge south' got 'You can't see any such thing.' I had to guess that plain directions work.
A wizard appeared, waved a wand and vanished, and my sword glowed and then stopped, with no explanation.
Attacking the basilisk got a witty reply that it was never really there.
I tried to take the Zork I copy and it wasn't real either. I didn't know what was real and what wasn't.

wished: A way to tell which things the wizard made up before I tried to use them.
Natural sentences like 'cross the bridge' to work.
A hint about what I'm supposed to be doing.

lines.line: Your hand closes on nothing, and your eye on less. It was never there: the Wizard's word put it in the room, and the room, having no say in the matter, let it, and has the grace to look embarrassed about it now.
lines.why: Funny, and it explained the wizard's trick.

lines.line: The room, which had been looking a little odd round the edges, settles down and is only a room.
lines.why: Showed the wizard's spell wearing off.

fun.why: The illusion jokes were charming, but I played too briefly to find a goal.

engagement.why: I was curious about the wizard but had no clear aim.

difficulty.why: Moving around was easy. The parser was picky about wording.

interestingness.why: Illusions that disappear when you touch them are a good idea.

prose.why: The wry narration for the illusions was well written. The room descriptions were plain.
